short: Sharing more state leaves an own-objective gap
statement: Amortization trade: moving computation from per-pair optimization into shared or per-style state lowers marginal cost by orders of magnitude; every audited within-paper comparison against per-pair or per-scene optimization reports a residual gap on the paper's own objective; comparisons against less-shared learned states usually do (CIN, AdaIN) but not always (StyleCrafter).

short: Unseen-style coverage depends on the training-style distribution
statement: Zero-shot coverage is distributional: performance on unseen styles depends on proximity to and size of the training style distribution, not on the arbitrary-reference interface.
The per-content term is not monotonically eliminated: inversion-based diffusion transfer reintroduces per-content (and per-reference) computation that can dominate per-pair cost.

short: Acquired states retain compatibility limits; no cross-family test in the coded sample
statement: Every acquired style state carries a compatibility domain (style set, base-checkpoint family, scene); positive transfer evidence is confined to the same base family or to warm starts, and no audited paper tests cross-family portability.

short: Composition interferes where states share a binding subspace
statement: Composition interference arises where acquired states share a binding subspace; it is asymmetric across factors and avoided only by explicit separation or low-dimensional statistic interpolation.

short: Cross-paper cost and quality orderings are not identified
statement: Cross-paper cost and quality orderings are not identified: the same method's runtime and rank change with implementation and with the metric's alignment to each method's objective.

short: Disentanglement relocates cost into acquisition or inference
statement: Interventions that reduce entanglement relocate cost into acquisition (paired data, staged fitting, human selection) or into per-sample inference (inversion, guidance).

short: Reported proxy metrics do not separately identify leakage and dilution
statement: The reported reference-similarity proxies do not separately identify removal of unwanted reference semantics and reduced intended style strength in the coded sample.

short: Representation, binding locus and acquisition are distinct leakage sources
statement: Leakage has at least three intervenable sources -- representation granularity, binding locus and acquisition objective; binding interventions are documented in all three non-objective carriers, acquisition interventions in parameter and condition carriers, representation interventions only in condition carriers of the audited set.

short: Leakage and dilution trade along a strength axis
statement: For a fixed representation and binding, leakage and dilution are opposite ends of a strength/weight axis; only frontier comparisons at matched operating points are informative.

short: Causal attributions of leakage conflict across papers
statement: Causal attributions of leakage conflict across papers (training objective versus representation versus routing) and are not resolved by any audited intervention.

short: ``Leakage'' names several phenomena; definition needs a style scope
statement: 'Leakage' names distinct phenomena (reference-to-output semantics, content-to-output style, sibling-to-sibling, iterated target erosion); its definition depends on a declared style scope.

short: Style factors are entangled in outputs and in metrics
statement: Style factors (colour, texture, layout) are bound through different mechanisms and are entangled both in outputs and in the metrics used to score content preservation.

short: Each coupling constrains a specific relation only
statement: Each coupling mechanism constrains a specific relation (visible flow trajectories, input-video correspondences, frozen shared geometry, a learned temporal prior), and evidence for it is confined to that relation.

short: Consistency scores depend on correspondence and may favor weakly stylized outputs
statement: Reported consistency scores depend on their correspondence system; selected comparisons favor static, blurred or weakly stylized outputs. Individual source observations are retained in the evidence register.

short: Selected comparisons link consistency gains to weaker style
statement: Selected comparisons show that improved consistency scores can coincide with weaker style fidelity; one recorded counterexample prevents a universal ordering.

short: Selected protocols leave reappearance and geometry preservation incompletely tested
statement: Occlusion/reappearance, long horizons, geometry change and joint time-view consistency are untested or only qualitatively shown in the audited set.

short: Shared 3D scenes do not uniformly beat 2D video methods
statement: Shared 3D scene representations do not uniformly outperform 2D video methods on reported metrics: they lead on short-range warped error but not consistently on long-range or reference-fidelity metrics.
